KR.read: Korea's oral_care segment now has domestic size data, not just trade flow, though the two RETAIL aggregator figures run in the wrong direction relative to each other: Grand View Research (via Daxue Consulting) puts the market at US$975.9mn for 2024, while Deep Market Insights puts a LATER year, 2025, at a LOWER US$892.82mn - roughly 1.19x apart once normal growth is allowed for, an unresolved definitional mismatch (both LOW confidence, neither states channel coverage or duty-free treatment). A MEDIUM-confidence MFDS PRODUCTION figure also exists, but narrowly scoped: KRW 405.1bn (2024, ~US$274.0mn) for 치약제 (dentifrice/toothpaste) only, since Korea regulates toothpaste as a quasi-drug rather than a cosmetic - this excludes toothbrushes, mouthwash and other formats, so it is well short of a full oral-care read; it is roughly 1.5x below Daxue/Grand View's retail figure, consistent with a retail-vs-production and import-coverage difference, not a conflict. Export figures are unchanged: US$0.079986bn HS3306 world exports (2024, HIGH), of which US$0.000251bn ([CORRIDOR]-tagged) went to India.
KR.trend: The two RETAIL forecast CAGRs agree closely despite disagreeing on level: Grand View/Daxue 6.9% (2025-2030, LOW) versus Deep Market Insights 6.41% (2026-2034, LOW), within about half a point of each other. Against that, a PRODUCTION-basis growth figure shows the opposite direction: Korean domestic toothpaste production FELL 3.27% in 2024 (ESTIMATE confidence, derived from two consecutive MFDS quasi-drug statistics releases) - a genuine contrary signal, flagged deliberately rather than smoothed over. Production and retail are different measures (factory-gate dentifrice-only output vs. retail sell-through across the whole category including imports), so a production decline alongside forecast retail growth is not a contradiction to resolve, though it may point to import substitution or a mix shift away from dentifrice - a hypothesis, not a settled finding.
KR.caveats: Do not read the -3.27% production figure as 'the' Korea oral care growth rate: it covers dentifrice production only and excludes imports, while the two positive forecast CAGRs describe retail demand across a wider category. The two RETAIL size figures disagree in the wrong direction (later year, lower level) and should not be averaged.

IN.read: India oral_care now has multiple RETAIL size reads that disagree, plus one that revised itself. IMARC: US$1.1bn (2025, LOW). The India Watch: INR 21,000cr (~US$2.18bn, 2025, LOW, trade publication with no disclosed methodology) - about 2.0x IMARC's figure for the same year. Renub Research: US$2.03bn (2024, LOW) in an earlier report, but the same publisher's later report page gives US$1.23bn (2025, LOW) - a roughly 40% downward revision with no stated definitional change; the later Renub figure sits closer to IMARC, the earlier one closer to The India Watch. A HIGH-confidence company figure now exists alongside these: Dabur India's Oral Care business declined 5.2% YoY in FY25 (RETAIL basis, secondary-sales/sell-through, BSE regulatory filing) - company-level, not the category, and the company's own investor deck attributes the decline to a high base effect (Q4FY24 oral care had grown 22% YoY); for context, Dabur's oral care business had grown 5.3% YoY in the prior quarter (Q2FY25), so this is not read as a sustained category downturn.
IN.trend: Three forecast CAGRs cluster more tightly than the size figures: IMARC 4.15% (2026-2034, LOW), Renub's earlier vintage 5.18% (2025-2033, LOW, off the US$2.03bn base), and Renub's later vintage 4.45% (2026-2034, LOW, off the US$1.23bn base) - the rates agree far better than the levels do. Dabur's -5.2% is the only observed year-on-year figure and is company-specific, explicitly attributed by the company to a prior-year high base rather than a category-wide slowdown.
IN.caveats: Renub Research revised its own India oral care size down about 40% between two published vintages with no stated definitional change - a publisher reliability signal, not just an ordinary cross-source gap. Dabur's -5.2% should not be read as a category-wide contraction: it is one company's branded secondary sales, explicitly base-effect-driven per the company's own commentary, and organised-market only.

combined.read: Both geographies now carry RETAIL size figures, but neither has one that is internally settled: Korea's two aggregator figures disagree by direction (a later year reading lower), and India's range from US$1.1bn to US$2.18bn across three sources, one of which revised itself ~40% between vintages. Given neither side offers a single defensible value_usd_bn, no KR-vs-IN size comparison is attempted here. The two [CORRIDOR]-tagged trade figures - Korea's ~US$0.000251bn FOB export to India versus India's ~US$0.000485bn CIF import from Korea - describe the same HS 3306 flow from opposite customs sides; the difference likely reflects the FOB/CIF basis gap and normal mirror-statistics discrepancy rather than two distinct quantities.
